gen_risks.description: Delays in enacting the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill could prevent the government from enforcing the statutory duty on schools to provide free breakfast clubs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Proceed with voluntary opt-in onboarding funded via Section 14 grants ahead of formal statutory enactment.
gen_risks.evidence: the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state-funded schools with primary-aged children to offer a free breakfast club

gen_risks.description: Delays or unexpected conditions in obtaining formal budget confirmation from HM Treasury could disrupt grant distribution and national rollout timing.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage proactively with HM Treasury through the project board and Major Projects Portfolio tracking to secure timely approvals.
gen_risks.evidence: The programme's success depends on several factors. These include timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury

gen_risks.description: The internal CRM system minimum-viable product (MVP) may not be ready by November 2025, delaying EOI processing for Cohort 1.
gen_risks.mitigation: Focus internal IT development strictly on critical EOI features for the MVP and establish manual processing fallbacks.
gen_risks.evidence: we would develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum-viable product from November 2025.

gen_risks.description: Physical space and facility constraints at primary school estates may prevent schools from hosting required breakfast club numbers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy technical estate advisers to evaluate school premises and advise on space optimization and facility adaptations.
gen_risks.evidence: continuing contracts of technical estate advisers to test what schools can do to mitigate any space constraints.

gen_risks.description: Transition delays between the end of the National School Breakfast Programme in July 2026 and Cohort 2 launch in September 2026 could leave a gap in provision.
gen_risks.mitigation: Guarantee places for all participating NSBP schools in Cohort 2 and streamline transfer processes prior to July 2026.
gen_risks.evidence: ensure they do not have a gap in provision after the closure of the NSBP in July 2026.

gen_risks.description: Eligible primary schools may refuse or delay joining the programme due to perceived administrative complexities or capacity constraints.
gen_risks.mitigation: Simplify funding rules to a predictable model (£1,000 start-up plus daily rates) and provide support through local authorities.
gen_risks.evidence: simplified, with a view to being easier to understand and fairer for schools. This should ease the burden and potentially increase willingness to engage

gen_risks.description: Standardized funding rates may not cover actual operational costs for schools facing unique staffing, food, or localized cost pressures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply Area Cost Adjustments and utilize findings from evaluation studies to review and adjust daily rate structures.
gen_risks.evidence: there will always be a level of uncertainty at an individual school level and on a day-to-day basis.

gen_risks.description: Uncertainty surrounding multi-year funding approvals beyond Year 1 could impair long-term strategic planning and school retention.
gen_risks.mitigation: Submit subsequent multi-year business cases early using preliminary evidence from Year 1 national rollout and early adopters.
gen_risks.evidence: Funding for future years will be agreed separately through business cases.

gen_risks.description: Shortages of skilled delivery staff or managerial capacity in DfE and schools could disrupt club operations and oversight.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated funding to local authorities and leverage education framework advisers to bolster local recruitment and management.
gen_risks.evidence: availability of skilled staff and resources, in both DfE and the education sector.

gen_risks.description: Schools may fail to maintain compliance with mandatory School Food Standards due to food cost inflation or procurement challenges.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide central procurement toolkits, standardized menus, and commercial advisor support to help schools meet standards cost-effectively.
gen_risks.evidence: Food provided must be in line with school food standards.

gen_risks.description: Delays or operational issues in setting up the call-centre pilot could hinder accurate data collection and attendance tracking.
gen_risks.mitigation: Accelerate commercial procurement timelines and utilize existing administrative data reporting mechanisms as an interim solution.
gen_risks.evidence: start commercial processes to begin a call-centre pilot to support data collection.

gt_risks.description: Lower value for money compared to the 'do minimum' option in year 1, due to the shorter funding period available for the preferred option's new cohorts of schools.
Delivery risks around staffing and food costs for schools newly onboarded to the free breakfast clubs programme.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated through early adopter (EA) scheme insights and support funding.

gt_risks.description: Uncertainty in the labour-market benefits (parental workforce participation gains) the programme is expected to deliver.
gt_risks.mitigation: Addressed through conservative assumptions in the economic modelling.
